titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spells 44, 45, 46, 50 and 93
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates XVI, XVII. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 105–111; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: Five short spells on Plates 16 and 17 of Ani's papyrus, written after Spells 58 and 59. Each keeps the dead man whole in the world below: not dying a second time (Spell 44), not rotting (Spell 45), not perishing (Spell 46), not coming to the slaughter-block of the gods (Spell 50), and not being ferried off to the east to the festivals of the rebels (Spell 93, followed by another spell to the same end). Ani speaks as Ra, as Osiris and as the son of Osiris, and names the parts of his body that are made firm. The words are short and often obscure, many signs in Budge's print are uncertain, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: spell · of · not · dying · again · in · the-necropolis
sentences.i: Spell for not dying again in the necropolis.
sentences.n: Spell 44 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt mt m nm in red, and m ẖrt-nṯr in black. rꜣ n tmt 'spell for not …' as in the spells before: the mouth with its stroke, water n, and t, the sledge tm (U15) with the owl m as complement and a second t (Budge: temt), the negative verb tm, whose verb follows in the negatival complement. mt 'dying' is the owl m and t with a small ring printed under the t (coded N33, approximate), here a classifier not identified: the verb mwt 'die', written without its w. m nm is the owl m, then a slender slanting rod, taken as the knife nm (T34, approximate), the owl m as complement and the papyrus roll: m nm 'again, a second time', an adverbial phrase whose make-up is not clear (Budge: em nem). If the rod is the ox-leg (F25), the scribe meant m wḥm 'anew', with the same sense. ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis' is the flag nṯr, written first out of respect, the loop r (coded D21, approximate) and the block ẖr (T28). To die a second time was to be destroyed in the world below after the first death on earth: the end the dead most feared.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: My cavern is opened. (Twice.)
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. ḏd in N 'said by N', as before: the cobra and the hand, then in, here the sign in (coded W25, approximate) with water n as complement. wsir is the low seat (coded Q2, approximate) over the eye, and ꜣny has the kneeling man with an arm raised as classifier. wnw is the hare wn (E34) with water n as complement, the chick w, and the hatched door (O31) over the low hooked sign (U15) as classifiers: the passive sḏm, 'is opened', with the w that the passive sometimes shows (Budge: unu). tpḥt·i 'my cavern' is p and t (the t printed under the p but read before it), the wick ḥ and t, a small house (coded O1, approximate) as classifier, and ·i. sp sn, the threshing floor sp and two strokes, tells the reader to say the words twice. The cavern is the tomb or the hollow of the world below: when it opens, the dead man can go out and in.

sentences.l: fall · the-spirits · within · the-darkness
sentences.i: The spirits fall within the darkness.
sentences.n: ḫr 'fall' is ḫ and r with a falling man (coded A15, approximate) as classifier, as in Spell 29: the sḏm·f, with its noun subject after it. ꜣḫw is the crested ibis ꜣḫ (G25) with ḫ as complement, the chick w and a dotted stroke (coded Z1): taken as the plural ꜣḫw 'spirits'. Budge reads 'light'; a word for light is written with the same ibis, but it usually has the sun as classifier, which is not printed here. The reading is doubtful. m ẖnw 'within' is the owl m and ẖnw 'the inside': the belly of an animal ẖ (F32), water n, the pot nw (W24) and the chick w, with a small house (coded O1, approximate). kkw 'darkness' is k twice and the chick w, with two strokes, not read, and the sky with a star hanging from it, the sign of night. Spirits or light, it is the night of the world below in which the speaker finds himself.

sentences.l: makes-known(?) · me · the-Eye · of-Horus
sentences.i: The Eye of Horus makes me known(?).
sentences.n: Budge prints seru-à as one group; it is split here into sr and wi (q re-indexed). The first sign of sr is uncertain: a low flat sign with a ring at one end and an upright at the other, coded as the sledge U15; Budge reads s, and the reading follows him. Then the mouth r and the papyrus roll, the classifier of things abstract: sr 'make known, foretell', a sḏm·f whose noun subject irt ḥr 'the Eye of Horus' comes at the end. wi, the chick w and the seated man, is the dependent pronoun 'me', which stands before a noun subject. Budge has 'hath arranged me'; the sense of sr here is doubtful. irt 'eye' is the eye ir with t and a stroke, and ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon alone. The Eye of Horus, torn out by Seth and made whole again, stands for every restoring of what was damaged.

sentences.l: has-hidden · me · with-you · Imperishable-Stars
sentences.i: He has hidden me in your keeping, you Imperishable Stars.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes iw ḫmw sk; read iḫmw-sk. Budge prints àmen-nuà as one group; it is split here into imn·n and wi (q re-indexed). imn 'hide' is the reed i and the game-board mn (Y5) with n as complement, and a man behind a wall (coded A5, approximate) as classifier; the next water n is the n of the sḏm·n·f. wi is the chick w with a stroke standing for the seated man. No subject is written after the verb: it is taken as Wepwawet still, 'he has hidden me'; Budge's 'I have hidden myself' would need ·i, which is not there. m-ꜥ·tn 'with you, in your keeping' is the owl m, a second owl drawn with the arm ꜥ in one ligature, and ·tn (t, water n, plural strokes). Budge prints the next three groups apart (àu χemu seku); they are joined here into one word (q re-indexed): iḫmw-sk 'those who do not know perishing'. It is the reed i; ḫ, the owl m and the chick w with the negative arms (coded D35, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers, the verb ḫm 'not know'; then sk 'perish', s, the cord sk (coded V29, approximate) with k as complement, a star, a stroke and a seated god. The chick after the reed has no place in the word and is not read; taken with Budge as a separate iw, the cry 'O!' or the particle, it hardly changes the sense. The Imperishable Stars are the stars round the pole that never set; the dead hoped to join them.

sentences.l: (iw) · brow(?)-my · (is)-as · Ra · (iw) · face-my · (is)-open
sentences.i: My brow(?) is Ra, and my face is open.
sentences.n: iw, the reed and the chick, opens this and the next statement and is not translated. Budge prints àpt (?) and the seated man as two groups, querying the first; they are joined here as wpt·i (q re-indexed). The first sign is a tall staff with a crossbar and a forked top, coded as the standard R15, approximate (S40 is also possible); then t, a stroke and a small curl taken as the flesh sign (F51, approximate), the classifier of parts of the body, and the seated man ·i, which Budge restores in brackets. The forked top is taken as the horns wp on a staff (the code R15 is only the nearest shape), and àp is how Budge reads the horns wp elsewhere (Àp-uat for wp-wꜣwt in line 2): wpt 'brow, forehead', written with wp, t and the stroke as in Spell 17, here with the flesh sign as well. The sign is not certain, and the reading is doubtful. m rꜥ is the m of predication, 'is (as) Ra': the sun-disc with a stroke and a seated god. ḥr·i 'my face' is the face with its stroke and ·i; wn 'open' is the hatched door (O31) over the low hooked sign (U15), the door here writing the whole word, a stative after its noun. The dead man's body is made divine part by part, and an open face is one that sees and is seen.

sentences.i: My heart is on its seat.
sentences.n: ḥꜣty·i 'my heart' as in Spell 27, the forepart of a lion ḥꜣt with t, two strokes y and the heart as classifier; but the suffix ·i is written with a seated wigged figure (coded A40), the sign of a god, not with the kneeling man. ḥr 'on' is the face with its stroke. st·f 'its seat' is the seat st (Q1) with t as complement, a small house (coded O1, approximate) as classifier, and the viper ·f. A heart on its seat is a heart in its place and at rest, the condition for thought and speech.

sentences.l: utterance-my · know-I
sentences.i: My utterance I know.
sentences.n: Budge prints ṭep and re-à as two groups; they are joined here into one word, tp-rꜣ·i (q re-indexed): the head tp and the mouth rꜣ, each with its stroke, and ·i. tp-rꜣ is 'utterance', literally 'the head (or tip) of the mouth'. rḫ·i 'I know' is the mouth r, the placenta ḫ and the papyrus roll as classifier, with ·i, which Budge restores in brackets: the sḏm·f. The object stands first, as if for emphasis; the order is unusual, and the sense ('I know what I have to say') is a guess. The dead needed the right words at every gate and before every god.

sentences.i: I am Ra, protecting himself by himself.
sentences.n: ink 'I' (the pot, the basket and the seated man) with a noun after it makes a sentence without a verb, 'I am Ra'; Ra is written with the seated god with the disc on his head (C1) alone. mkt is the owl m, the arm, k and t (Budge: māket, 'verily'); the arm carries no sound here and is a classifier, as in mkt 'protection' in Spell 147. It is taken as mkt, the infinitive of mki 'protect', which ends in t, with sw as its object; the construction is unusual, and the reading is doubtful. sw 'him' is the sedge sw with w as complement, the dependent pronoun as object, and ḏs·f 'himself' is the cobra ḏ, the bolt s and ·f, as in Spell 27. The sun-god, who came into being by himself, needs no other to guard him.

sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir rḫ rꜣ pn n ḥwꜣ·f m in red; ẖrt-nṯr and wsir are in black. ir 'if' is the reed and the mouth; rḫ (the mouth, the placenta ḫ and the papyrus roll) is the passive sḏm, 'is known', with rꜣ pn 'this spell' as its subject, as at the end of Spell 58. ḥwꜣ·f 'he rots' has here the papyrus roll after the ringed oval, and the viper ·f. ẖrt-nṯr is written out: the flag, the block ẖr (T28) over r and t, and the hills as classifier, where the title has the short group. The last word, wsir, stands alone: it may be the start of 'the Osiris Ani' with the name left unwritten, and it is given as it stands. Spell 45 ends here.

sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red. i 'O' is the reed with a man raising his hands to his face (A2). ḥwnw 'youths, children' is the wick ḥ, the hare wn with n, the pot nw and the coil w repeating its sounds, and a seated child with hand to mouth (coded A17, approximate), the kneeling man and a stroke as classifiers (Budge: ḥunnu). šw 'Shu', the god of the air, is the feather šw (H6) with w and a seated god; sp sn, restored in brackets by Budge, repeats the call. dwꜣt is the star dwꜣ (N14) with ꜣ and a small house (coded O1, approximate) as classifier, without t: taken as the Duat, the world below, in a direct genitive; Budge's 'place of the dawn' (dwꜣ is also 'morning') is possible, and the reading is doubtful. sḫm 'have power over' (with m) is the sceptre sḫm (S42) with s, m and ḫ as complements and a small bird with arms (coded G24, approximate) as classifier: a participle, 'who have power'. sšd·f is the bolt s, two looped cords (coded V6, approximate) with the hand d between them, and ·f: taken as sšd 'fillet, headband' (Budge: 'diadem'). m ḥnmmt 'among the Henmemet' is the disc with falling rays (coded N8, approximate), which writes ḥnmmt, with m twice as complement (the owl and the sign m), t, the kneeling man, a seated god and a stroke as classifiers (Budge: hamemet). sentences.n: Spell 50 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt ꜥq r in red and nmmt nṯr in black; the water n of n is restored in brackets by Budge. ꜥq 'enter' is the arm ꜥ (printed as a flat line with an upright tab), the triangle q (N29) and the walking legs, the negatival complement after tmt; ꜥq r 'enter into'. nmmt 'the block' is a domed block with a knife laid across it (coded T29), which writes the word alone (Budge: nemmat). Budge prints the flag and the seated god in the same group and takes them as classifiers; they are split off here as nṯr 'god', the flag with the seated god as in ḥtp-nṯr at the end of Spell 93 A, in a direct genitive: nmmt nṯr 'the block of the god', the slaughter-block of the gods. There the enemies of the gods were cut up; the dead man must not come to it.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris Ani: My nape is knit together for me in heaven by Ra, the keeper(?) of the earth.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏd in in red; in is written here with the reed and water n. Budge prints θesu-nà as one group; it is split here into ṯs·w and n·i (q re-indexed). ṯs 'tie, knit together' is the girdle knot ṯs (S24) with the coil w under it and the low hooked sign (U15) as classifier: the passive sḏm with its w, 'is tied'. ḥꜣ·i 'my nape, the back of my head' is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ (M16) with ꜣ as complement, a small head (coded D1, approximate) and a stroke as classifiers, and ·i: the noun from which the preposition ḥꜣ 'behind' comes. m pt 'in heaven' is the sign m and the sky. iry is the reed, the mouth r and two strokes y, with a seated wrapped man holding a stick (coded A47, approximate), the sign of a guard, and the papyrus roll: taken as iry 'keeper', with tꜣ 'the earth' (the strip of land, coded N16, approximate) after it. in 'by' names the agent, and rꜥ 'Ra' is r and the arm ꜥ with the seated god with the disc. How iry tꜣ stands in the sentence is not clear: it may be a title of Ra, as taken here, or 'what belongs to the earth'. The knitting of neck to head is what the slaughter-block would undo.

sentences.i: It was given(?) on the day of making firm my raising up from weariness upon the legs, on that day … of the cutting off of the hair.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ṯsnw·i; read ṯsw·i. rdit is the mouth r, t and the arm (D36, no loaf in the hand): the infinitive of rdi 'give', here without a subject, perhaps as a heading, and rendered 'it was given'; the form and the sense are doubtful (Budge: 'it hath been granted'). hrw 'day' is the courtyard h (O4), r, w, the sun and a stroke, an adverb of time without a preposition, as often. smnt 'making firm' is the bolt s, the game-board mn with n, a tall hooked staff (coded S38, approximate; a classifier not identified), t and the papyrus roll: the infinitive of smn 'make firm, establish', after the genitive n. ṯsw·i is the girdle knot ṯs with water n printed under it, the coil w, the low hooked sign and ·i; the water n has no place in the word and is not read (Budge has none), and ṯs is taken in its sense 'raise up', 'my raising up'. r nnyw 'from weariness' is two rushes and two water n's (nn), two reeds y and the chick w, with the weary man (coded A7, approximate), the small bird and plural strokes: nni 'be weary, inert', the state of the dead before they are raised. ḥr mnty 'upon the two legs' is the game-board mn with n, t, two strokes and two legs, the dual of mnt 'thigh, leg'. After pfy 'that' (the stool p, the viper f, two strokes) Budge prints at the head of line 3 a sign he does not read and does not translate (coded R3, approximate: a bar on a small foot with two knobbed uprights); it is joined here to pfy as an unread sign (q re-indexed). The genitive nt that follows is feminine, which hrw is not: the unread sign may be a feminine noun we cannot now read. ḥsq 'cut off' is the wick ḥ, s and the triangle q (N29), with the knife and the low hooked sign as classifiers. smꜣt is the lung and windpipe smꜣ (coded F36) with a stroke, m, t and hanging tresses as classifier: a word for the hair of the head (Budge: samet). The day of cutting the hair is not explained; cutting the hair was a sign of mourning.

sentences.n: ṯs 'tie' is the girdle knot with s as complement and the low hooked sign: the passive sḏm, 'has been tied'. ṯst 'vertebra, backbone' is the knot with t and a stroke, the noun from ṯs (Budge: θest, 'the vertebrae'), in a direct genitive with ḥꜣ·i 'my nape', written here without the vulture. in 'by' names the agents. stẖ 'Seth' is the bolt and a hatched rectangle (coded N37, approximate, by house ruling) with a seated god: the sign under the bolt stands for the rest of the name. psḏt nṯrw 'the Ennead of the gods' is the loaf (X6), which writes psḏt, with t, and the flag three times; no 'and' is written between Seth and the Ennead. m wsr·s tpy 'in their first strength': wsr 'strength' is the head and neck of an animal wsr (F12) with s and r and the low hooked sign; ·s 'her, its' looks back to the Ennead, a feminine noun; tpy 'first' is the head tp with a stroke and two strokes y; Budge prints the numeral 4 inside wsr·s. That Seth, the murderer of Osiris, should tie the dead man's neck is striking; the spell does not explain it.

sentences.i: My vertebra has been tied by Nut, who saw at her first occasion, who sees right order, when the gods had not yet been born in their forms.
sentences.n: ṯs·w 'has been tied' is the girdle knot with the coil w, over the bolt s and the low hooked sign: the passive sḏm with w, as in line 1; ṯst·i 'my vertebra' has the seated man ·i. in 'by' is written with the reed first, then the sign in (coded W25, approximate). mꜣꜣ is the eye with the sickle and two vultures; mꜣꜣt adds t. Both are taken as participles describing Nut, the second with the feminine ending, the first without it; mꜣꜣ may instead be the infinitive, 'seeing'. sp·s tpy 'her first occasion' is the bolt s, the stool p and the threshing floor sp as classifier, the bolt ·s 'her', and tpy 'first' (the head tp, the stool p as complement, two strokes y): the first time, the beginning of the world. mꜣꜥt 'right order' is the sickle mꜣ, the arm ꜥ, t, the plinth mꜣꜥ (Aa11) and a roll (coded Y1, approximate) over plural strokes. n is the negative arms with water n as complement; with msi 'bear, be born' (the three fox-skins ms with s, and a seated woman giving birth, coded B3, approximate, as classifier) it is the passive in the past, 'the gods had not (yet) been born'. ꜥšmw is the arm ꜥ (printed flat; Budge reads a), the pool š (coded N37, approximate), the owl m, the chick w and a falcon with a flail (G6) as classifier: ꜥšm 'form, image of a god' (Budge: aśemu, 'visible forms'). Nut, the sky, was there before the gods she bore; the dead man is knit together by the oldest of powers.

sentences.n: Spell 93 begins. The papyrus writes rꜣ n tmt rdit ḏꜣ·tw in red, s in black, r iꜣbt m in red, and ẖrt-nṯr in black. rdit 'letting' as in Spell 27: the mouth r, t and the arm (no loaf). ḏꜣ·tw is the fire-drill ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate) with ꜣ as complement, a boat-like sign on a low base (coded P1, approximate; the sign is unsure) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, and the tw of the passive: 'letting (a man) be ferried', from ḏꜣi 'cross, ferry over'. s 'a man' is the bolt, a stroke and the seated man. iꜣbt 'the east' is the standard of the east iꜣb (R15) with b and t. The east, where the sun rises, is here the place of the festivals of the rebels, as the spell goes on to say, and the dead man must not be carried there.

sentences.n: The papyrus writes nwy; read pwy. ḏd in is in red; in is the reed and water n. i 'O' is the reed with a man raising one arm (coded A26, approximate). ḥnnw 'phallus' is the wick ḥ, a long blade with a crosspiece (coded U7, approximate) where the plant ḥn is expected, water n, the pot nw and the chick w, with the phallus (D52) as classifier (Budge: ḥennu); in line 6 of the next spell the same word has the plant ḥn (M2). The demonstrative is printed with the pot nw where the stool p should be (Budge: nui, 'that'); the same phrase, ḥnnw pwy n rꜥ, is written with the stool in the next spell, and the sense allows only pwy 'this'. n rꜥ 'of Ra': water n and the seated god with the disc. nwd is water n, the adze nw (coded U19, approximate) with the pot nw and the chick w, then a long rounded bar (coded Y1, approximate) and the walking legs, both restored by Budge in brackets: the bar is taken as the flat hand d, as Budge reads it (ennuṭ, 'advancing'), and the word as nwd 'turn, move', a participle; the reading is doubtful. ḥḏ·f is the mace ḥḏ (T3) with a cobra ḏ wound round it, the crossed sticks and the small bird as classifiers, and ·f: ḥḏ 'damage, destroy', a sḏm·f, 'it destroys'. ḫnnw 'strife' as in Spell 50. The phallus of Ra is the sun's power to beget, called on here against disorder.

sentences.i: Now I shall not be carried off to the east to perform the festivals of the rebels there, with evil cutting, with (ḥst?), with binding(?) of the horns.
sentences.n: ir again, and n, the negative arms alone, here for nn as in Spell 44. iṯ 'seize, carry off' is the tether (coded V13, approximate) on a small stand, t for ṯ and the low hooked sign, with ·i written before the tw of the passive and read after it, as in Spell 44. iꜣbtt 'the east' has here two t's and the hills as classifier. r irt 'to perform' is r with the infinitive irt, the eye and t. ḥbw 'festivals' is the wick ḥ and the leg b with the alabaster basin ḥb (W3), the sun and plural strokes. sbiw 'rebels' is s, b and the reed, with a throw-stick (coded T14, approximate), a small ring (coded N33, approximate) and plural strokes: the enemies of the sun. im 'there' is the reed and the owl. Three phrases with m 'with' follow. šꜥd ḏwt 'evil cutting': šꜥd is the pool š (coded N37, approximate), the arm ꜥ and the hand d, with a stem with side-shoots (coded M3, approximate), the knife and a stroke as classifiers (Budge: śāṭ, 'gashings'); ḏwt 'evil' is the mountain ḏw with t, w, the small bird and plural strokes. ḥst is the wick ḥ, the jar ḥs (coded W14, approximate), s, t and the walking legs: a word not known, and Budge's 'shutting in on every side' is a guess. nwḥt is water n, the adze nw (coded U19, approximate) with the pot and the chick, ḥ, t and two strokes, taken as nwḥ 'bind with a rope', 'binding'; ḥnwty is the two horns written alone (F16 twice), read with Budge as the dual of ḥnwt 'horn' (Budge: ḥennuti; ꜥbwy 'the two horns' is also possible). Budge has 'goring by the horns', and the reading is doubtful. A beast for sacrifice was led and bound by its horns: at the festivals of the rebels the enemies of Ra are slaughtered like cattle, and the dead man must not be taken there as a victim.

(particle; sometimes written ẖr) · also 'from' (of persons: ḫr s nty·f ḫr·f 'from the man with whom it is')
glossary.ꜣḫ: ꜣḫ — spirit, the glorified and effective dead (noun; written with the crested ibis) · also glory, effective power (noun m.) · also glorious, effective (adjective) · also to be glorious, be effective, be an effective spirit (verb) · also ꜣḫt, what is effective or useful, a benefit (noun f.) · also ꜣḫ n, to be of use to, serve, benefit (someone) (verb)
glossary.ẖnw: ẖnw — the inside, interior, residence (noun; m ẖnw 'within')
glossary.kkw: kkw — darkness (noun m.; written with the sign of night; Budge: keku)
glossary.sr: sr — official, magistrate, noble (noun; plural srw) · a second word of the same spelling: to foretell, make known (verb; Budge: sert)
glossary.wi: wi — me (1st person singular dependent pronoun, object of a verb)
glossary.irt: irt — eye (noun f.; dual irty 'the two eyes')
glossary.ḥr: ḥr — face; (preposition) upon, on, over, concerning · a second word of the same spelling: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru) · also 'at' (ḥr sbꜣw 'at the gates'); ḥr-tp 'upon' (compound preposition: ḥr + tp 'head') · also for, on behalf of; on account of (preposition; ḥr·k 'for you') · also 'with' (of the cause of a feeling: ḥtp ḥr·s 'content with it')
glossary.rnn: rnn — to nurse, bring up (a child) (verb; written with the woman holding a child as classifier)
glossary.sḏm·n·f: sḏm·n·f — the n of the sḏm·n·f, marking a completed action ("I have …", "I …ed") (verb form; written between the verb and its suffix)
glossary.wp-wꜣwt: wp-wꜣwt — Wepwawet, 'Opener of the Ways', a jackal god (god's name; Budge: Àp-uat)
glossary.imn: imn — to hide, conceal; to be hidden (verb)
glossary.m-ꜥ: m-ꜥ — from (the hand of); with, in the keeping of; through, by (compound preposition: m 'in' + ꜥ 'hand')
glossary.·tn: ·tn — you, your (2nd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.iḫmw-sk: iḫmw-sk — 'those who do not know perishing', the Imperishable Stars (plural noun, from ḫm 'not know' and sk 'perish'; written with a star as classifier; Budge: àu χemu seku, 'never setting stars')
glossary.iw: iw — opens a statement, often with a suffix (iw·f "he …"); not translated (particle)
glossary.wpt: wpt — brow, forehead; top of the head (noun f.; written with the horns; Budge: àpt)
glossary.rꜥ: rꜥ — Ra, the sun-god (god's name; Budge: Rā) · also the sun; day (noun; rꜥ nb 'every day')
glossary.ḥꜣty: ḥꜣty — heart, breast (noun; written with the forepart of a lion, ḥꜣt)
glossary.st: st — place, seat, throne (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: it, them (3rd person dependent pronoun, object of a verb, written s-t) · also, with the hill-country sign, the desert hills, the necropolis (?) (noun; sense uncertain) · the dependent pronoun is also written with s alone
glossary.·f: ·f — he, him, his, it (3rd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the horned viper) · after a dual noun sometimes followed by the two strokes of the dual, which are not read (ꜥwy·f 'his two arms')
glossary.tp-rꜣ: tp-rꜣ — utterance, what is said (noun m.; literally 'head (or tip) of the mouth')
glossary.ink: ink — I (1st person singular independent pronoun; ink N "I am N")
glossary.mki: mki — to protect, guard (verb; infinitive mkt; Budge: māket)
glossary.sw: sw — he, him, it (3rd person masculine singular dependent pronoun)
glossary.ḏs: ḏs — self (noun; with a suffix, ḏs·f 'himself, by himself, of his own accord')
glossary.n: n — not; negates the verb ('I have not …') · also in n wn "there is not" · a second word of the same spelling: the preposition "to, for" (n·i "to me") · the negative also before a noun, 'without, there being no …' · the preposition also 'because of, on account of'
glossary.ḫm: ḫm — not to know, be ignorant of (verb; passive ḫm·tw 'be unknown, be ignored'; in iḫmw-sk 'those who do not know perishing'; Budge: χem)
glossary.·tw: ·tw — one, someone (impersonal suffix; makes a passive: ḏd·tw 'one says, it is said')
glossary.ꜥnḫ: ꜥnḫ — to live; life (verb) · also living (participle or adjective after its noun; bꜣ ꜥnḫ 'a living ba')
glossary.·k: ·k — you, your (2nd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the basket sign)
glossary.itf: itf — father (noun m.; plural itw 'fathers, forefathers')
glossary.sꜣ: sꜣ — protection (noun; m sꜣ "for the protection of") · a second word of the same spelling: son (noun m.; the pintail-duck sign; sꜣ·k 'your son', sꜣ tpy 'eldest son') · a third word of the same spelling: back (noun; the sign Aa18; as in m-sꜣ 'behind'; Budge: sa)
glossary.nwt: nwt — Nut, the sky-goddess, mother of the sun and of Osiris (god's name; Budge: Nut) · a second word of the same spelling: bonds, wrappings (?) (noun f. plural; Budge: netu) · a third word (?): a weapon or tool (noun f.; doubtful; Budge: nut(?))
glossary.wr: wr — great (adjective); a great one, a great amount (noun)
glossary.štꜣ: štꜣ — secret, hidden; štꜣw "secret things, mysteries" (adjective) · also to be hidden, hide (verb)
glossary.ḫꜥ: ḫꜥ — to appear in glory, rise (verb; of a king on his throne, a god, the sun)
glossary.·kwi: ·kwi — I (1st person singular ending of the stative: "I am …, I have …")
glossary.ḥwꜣ: ḥwꜣ — to rot, decay (verb; the noun ḥwꜣw is 'rottenness'; written with the classifier of swelling and decay; Budge: ḥua)
glossary.wrd: wrd — to be weary, tired (verb); wrd-ib 'Weary of heart', a name of the dead Osiris (Budge: urṭ; reading doubtful here)
glossary.·s: ·s — she, her, it, its (3rd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the folded cloth or the bolt)
glossary.dꜣ: dꜣ — to go away, disappear (?) (verb of going; the sense is a guess; Budge: ṭa, 'disappear')
glossary.bn: bn — to depart, go away (?) (verb; written with the walking legs; the sense is a guess; Budge: ben, 'depart')
glossary.·st: ·st — it, they (suffix pronoun of the 3rd person; a writing of ·s with t found in later texts; doubtful)
glossary.ir: ir — to do, make (lemma iri) · a second word of the same spelling: the particle ir "when, if" at the head of a clause (ir ꜥq·i "when I entered"), here apparently also bringing in a question ("do you know …?") · also "as for" (particle; ir with a noun puts that noun first as the topic)
glossary.mi: mi — come! (the imperative that serves the verbs of coming, iwi and ii; in later copies written with the owl m and the forearm ꜥ, as if mꜥ, with the walking legs) · a second word of the same spelling: like, as (preposition)
glossary.pn: pn — this (masculine demonstrative, after its noun)
glossary.sk: sk — to wipe, sweep (verb); perhaps also to drag, tow (?) (sense uncertain; Budge's 'toweth') · a second word of the same spelling: to perish (verb; skt after tm 'not perishing'; the Imperishable Stars iḫmw-sk are 'those who do not know perishing')
glossary.wnn: wnn — to be, exist (verb; wn·n·i "I have been"; n wn "there is not")
glossary.i: i — O!, hail (the vocative interjection that opens each declaration)
glossary.ḥwn: ḥwn — youth, child (noun m.; plural ḥwnw 'youths'; Budge: ḥunnu)
glossary.šw: šw — empty, lacking, free (of) (adjective; verb šwi 'be empty') · a second word of the same spelling: Shu, god of the air, who holds up the sky (god's name; Budge: Śu)
glossary.dwꜣt: dwꜣt — the Duat, the underworld through which the sun and the dead pass by night (noun f.; place name; Budge: Ṭuat)
glossary.sḫm: sḫm — power, might; sacred image, cult statue (noun) · also the verb 'prevail, have power (over: m)' (sḫm m 'have power over') · also Sekhem, Letopolis, a city of Horus north of Memphis (place name; Budge: Seχem)
glossary.sšd: sšd — a word not identified here (meaning uncertain; Budge: seśeṭ, sic) · to bind up, bandage (?) (verb; a guess; Budge: seśeṭ, 'bandaged') · a second word of the same spelling: fillet, headband (noun m.; Budge: 'diadem')
glossary.ḥnmmt: ḥnmmt — the Henmemet, a class of beings who live in the sun's light (noun f., collective; written with the disc with falling rays; Budge: hamemet)
glossary.wnwn: wnwn — to move about, roam (?) (verb, reduplicated; written with the walking legs; the sense is doubtful; Budge: unun, 'travel')
glossary.ꜥq: ꜥq — to enter, go in (verb; ꜥq r "enter into")
glossary.r: r — to, towards, into, at (preposition); with an infinitive "in order to"; with the sḏmt·f "until"; after an imperative, with a suffix (ir·k), "yourself, then" · a second word of the same spelling: goose, fowl (noun; the goose sign) · also against (of hostility: r·i 'against me'); concerning, about (r·f 'concerning him') · also 'than' (after an adjective or verb of quality, in a comparison: btnw r ṯsmw 'swifter than hounds') · also 'from' (of separation: ḫnr … r 'shut away from')
glossary.nmmt: nmmt — 'the block, the place of slaughter/execution'
glossary.ṯs: ṯs — to tie, knot; to raise up; to marshal, command (verb)
glossary.ḥꜣ: ḥꜣ — behind, around, about (preposition; Budge: ḥa) · a second word of the same spelling: back of the head, nape (noun m.; ḥꜣ·i 'my nape'; the noun from which the preposition comes)
glossary.iry: iry — one who belongs to, keeper of (nisba of r "to"; iry ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper") · also as an adjective, 'belonging to, pertaining to' (feminine irt; irt·f 'which belongs to him')
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.rdi: rdi — to give, put, place; with a sḏm·f, to cause, let (verb; di·f pr·i "he let me come forth")
glossary.hrw: hrw — terror, dread · a second word of the same spelling: day (noun; plural hrww)
glossary.smn: smn — to make firm, establish (verb; causative of mn 'be firm'; Budge: smen)
glossary.nni: nni — to be weary, inert, slack (verb; the state of the dead before they are raised; participle nnw 'the inert'; written with the weary man as classifier)
glossary.mnt: mnt — daily (adverb; Budge: ment) · a second word of the same spelling: thigh, leg (?) (noun f.; with the leg as classifier; Budge: ment, 'leg')
glossary.pf: pf — that (masculine demonstrative, after its noun; fem. tf)
glossary.ḥsq: ḥsq — to cut off (verb; written with the knife as classifier; perhaps also of cutting grain, reaping (?); Budge: ḥesq)
glossary.smꜣt: smꜣt — place of union (?) (noun f.; from smꜣ 'unite'; perhaps the tomb; Budge: samat) · a second word of the same spelling: hair of the head, tresses (noun f.; written with hanging tresses as classifier; Budge: samet)
glossary.ṯst: ṯst — vertebra, backbone (noun f.; from ṯs 'tie'; Budge: θest, 'the vertebræ')
glossary.stẖ: stẖ — Seth, god of storm and disorder, who murdered Osiris (god's name; written stẖ or swt; Budge: Sut)
glossary.psḏt: psḏt — the Ennead, the company of nine gods (noun f.; psḏt nṯrw 'the Ennead of the gods'; Budge: paut)
glossary.wsr: wsr — power, strength (noun); to be strong, powerful (verb); strong (adjective) · a second word of the same spelling: oar (noun m.; plural wsrw, written with the wood classifier; Budge: useru)
glossary.tpy: tpy — first, foremost, eldest (adjective; nisba of tp 'head'; sꜣ tpy 'eldest son')
glossary.ḫpr: ḫpr — to come into being, happen, become (verb)
glossary.swḏꜣ: swḏꜣ — to make sound, keep whole, preserve (verb; causative of wḏꜣ 'be sound, whole')
glossary.smꜣ: smꜣ — to slay, kill · also smꜣwt, place of killing (?) (noun f.; Budge: samatu)
glossary.iṯi: iṯi — to take, seize, take possession of (verb 3ae-inf; participle iṯ 'who took')
glossary.mꜣꜥt: mꜣꜥt — truth, right order (maꜥat) · also Maat, the goddess of truth and right order (god's name; the seated goddess with the feather)
glossary.msi: msi — to give birth; (passive) to be born (verb)
glossary.ꜥšm: ꜥšm — form, image of a god (noun m.; plural ꜥšmw; Budge: aśemu, 'visible forms')
glossary.pnty: pnty — Penty, a god (god's name; perhaps 'he who belongs to …', but the sense of the name is unknown; Budge: Penti)
glossary.ꜥꜣ: ꜥꜣ — great (adjective); (adverb) here, hither · a second word of the same spelling: donkey, ass (noun) · a third word of the same spelling: door, door-leaf (noun; iry-ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper") · also greatly, very (adverb, after an adjective or participle: ḥsy ꜥꜣ 'greatly favoured') · dual ꜥꜣwy 'the two doors, the double door' (noun; written with the door-leaf twice)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.iꜣbtt: iꜣbtt — the east, the eastern quarter where the sun rises (noun f.)
glossary.ḥnn: ḥnn — phallus (noun m.; also written ḥnnw)
glossary.pwy: pwy — this, that (masculine demonstrative, after its noun; hrw pwy 'that day')
glossary.nwd: nwd — to turn, bend, move (?) (verb; reading and sense doubtful; Budge: ennuṭ, 'advancing')
glossary.ḥḏ: ḥḏ — to damage, defraud, diminish · a second word of the same spelling: white, bright (adjective; verb 'be white, bright'; written with the mace)
glossary.ḫt: ḫt — thing, things, property (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: wood, tree, stick, a wooden board (noun m.) · a third word: stairway, terrace (?) (noun; written with the stairway sign; Budge: χet, 'steps') · a fourth word: rear, following (noun; m-ḫt 'after', imyw-ḫt 'those in the following of') · a fifth word: fire, flame (noun; written with the flame as classifier; Budge: χet) · also a rod as a measure of length (?) (noun; Budge: χet)
glossary.ḥḥ: ḥḥ — a million, countless (number); Heh, the god of endlessness
glossary.bꜣby: bꜣby — Babi, a savage baboon god who devours the condemned (god's name; Budge: Baabi) · also written bby, without the vulture (Budge: Bebi) · Budge also: Bàbà
glossary.im: im — there, therein (adverb; nty im "he who is there")
glossary.nn: nn — not, there is not (negative particle; nn + noun 'there is no …'; nn + sḏm·f 'will not …', the negative of the future; nn with a sentence without a verb 'there is not, … is not') · a second word of the same spelling: these, those (demonstrative pronoun before its noun, in classical Egyptian joined to it by the genitive n, nn n X; in later texts also without it) · the demonstrative also written nnw; perhaps also standing first in a sentence without a verb, 'this is …' (?)
glossary.sbiw: sbiw — rebel, the rebel serpent, enemy of the sun-god (noun m.; from sbi 'rebel'; Budge: Sebàu)
glossary.šꜥd: šꜥd — to cut, cut off (verb; infinitive šꜥd 'a cutting')
glossary.ḏw: ḏw — evil, bad; an evil deed (adjective, noun; written with the mountain ḏw)
glossary.ḥst: ḥst — a word not known (noun; Budge: ḥeset, 'shutting in on every side', a guess)
glossary.nwḥ: nwḥ — to bind with a rope, tie (verb); nwḥt 'binding' (noun f.; doubtful; Budge: ennuḥti, 'goring')
glossary.ḥnwt: ḥnwt — deceit, wrongdoing (exact reading uncertain; the sin is acting deceitfully) · a second word of the same spelling: mistress (noun f.; a title of goddesses, ḥnwt tꜣwy 'mistress of the Two Lands'; Budge: ḥent) · a second word of the same spelling: horn (noun f.; dual ḥnwty 'the two horns'; doubtful; Budge: ḥennuti)
glossary.ꜥm: ꜥm — to swallow, eat (verb; Budge: àmu 'eat')
glossary.rm: rm — fish (noun m.; plural rmw, written with the fish sign; Budge: remu)
glossary.db: db — to gore, butt, pierce with the horns (?) (verb; written with the two horns as classifier; Budge: ṭeb, 'pierce')
glossary.ky: ky — other, another (adjective; ky ḏd 'another saying', which brings in a variant explanation)
glossary.nb: nb — lord, master, possessor (of); (adjective, after a noun) every, all
glossary.irf: irf — then, now (enclitic particle, from r + ·f; mostly in questions, 'what then?', also after a statement or a command)
glossary.ḏꜣḏꜣ: ḏꜣḏꜣ — head (noun m.; written with the fire-drill twice and a head; Budge: t'at'a)
glossary.ist: ist — now, see (particle opening a new statement)
glossary.ii: ii — to come (verb; ii·n·i "I have come")
glossary.wšb: wšb — to answer, reply (verb; written with the man with hand to mouth as classifier of speech; Budge: us[eb], 'speak')
glossary.·sn: ·sn — they, them, their (3rd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.ḫpri: ḫpri — Khepri, 'he who comes into being', the sun-god at dawn, shown as a scarab (god's name; from ḫpr 'come into being'; Budge: χeperà)
glossary.kꜣ: kꜣ — ka, the life-force that receives offerings (noun); plural kꜣw, perhaps also "food, sustenance" · a second word of the same spelling: bull (noun; written with the bull) · a second word of the same spelling: then, so (particle, looking to the future)
glossary.bnnt: bnnt — sickness, disease (?) (noun f.; written with the classifier of swelling and disease; Budge: benentu)
glossary.itm: itm — Atum, 'the Complete One', the creator god of Heliopolis (god's name; Budge: Tem) · Budge also: Tmu
glossary.ḥtm: ḥtm — to destroy; to perish, be destroyed (verb; causative sḥtm; Budge: ḥetem)
glossary.ḥsb: ḥsb — to reckon, count; sš ḥsb "accounting scribe" (verb)
glossary.ḥtp-nṯr: ḥtp-nṯr — god's offerings, the offerings of a temple (noun)
glossary.nfr: nfr — beautiful, good, perfect (adjective; follows its noun; verb 'be good'); also beauty, goodness (noun m.)
glossary.imꜣḫ: imꜣḫ — honour, reverence; the honoured state of the blessed dead (noun; nb imꜣḫ "possessor of honour")
